items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: Because Lane used to come get me when I was in short pants. Yeah. That's where I started with Lane.

ctx.x: Did you ever play in Papa Lane's band? No, no.
Because Lane used to come get me when I was in short pants. Yeah. That's where I started with Lane. I was in short pants. What kind of job? He's living here too. Yeah. He's still alive.
What kind of job did Lane get?

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: He used to sleep at our house when he had to go on jobs like that.

ctx.x: Johnny Lala was a good friend of mine. I used to play with him in Brownlee's band. Yeah,

he's nice. He's a wonderful fellow. He's a good boy. He used to sleep at our house when he had to go on jobs like that. And they was afraid they wouldn't get up because he worked late at the market. He would take

sleep than they had upstairs you know. And they had cots up there. They were sleeping. Yeah. Gentlemen that fellow used to raise more Santa power at night and keep pillaging for them. Fetish scattered off.

items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1958-09-24
items.q: Oh, then Jacqueline caught ahold of me. Oh, well he caught me, man.

ctx.x: And did your father play ragtime?

Well, in them days there was what you call, it wasn't ragtime in them days. My father did. You know, it was dance fans, you know, but there wasn't no pep, you know? It was a regular, legitimate resistance, you see? Of course, they played with what was called ragtime in them days, but none of them was out there the Negroes. You see, my daddy gave it up. My daddy gave up music out when I was about ten years old, you see? You know, I'll never forget I was a young kid. First time I stood out all night, played with a…
I'm not going to be a man. I'm not going to be a man. I'm not going to be a man. I'm not going to be a man.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1957-03-26
items.q: And then got Johnny Lawler and boys like that in another place.

ctx.x: Was Vega a ragtime player or what did you

read on it? Oh, very good ragtime player. Very good. Very good. Yeah. In fact, as I'm telling you, well, him and Manuel Marlowe, in fact, were the first two kids that I picked up on horn. Then I began to get my boy, my boy, practicing and wanting it on this fellow, Mead and Perkins, pulled him through. And then got Johnny Lawler and boys like that in another place. Well, Brunus and all, they used to be with me all the time, the Brunus boys. The Brunus boys, especially Georgie Brunus, Georgie Brunus never left my…
Did they play regular cornets in those days or were they different?
